name: Descendents
label: SST
lede: A fisherman's kid, a mailman in his thirties and a biology nerd with glasses built pop-punk's blueprint in a South Bay rehearsal room, then kept pausing it for grad school.

eras.title: Two acoustic guitars in Manhattan Beach
eras.text: Descendents started as Frank Navetta's idea, not a hardcore band at all: surf-pop songs written on acoustic guitars in the South Bay. The pieces that mattered arrived fast, a 15-year-old drummer who fished for a living and a bass player twice his age.

years.h: Frank Navetta and David Nolte start The Itch
years.p: Frank Navetta and David Nolte write songs on acoustic guitars in Manhattan Beach, California. Navetta soon renames the project Descendents; by year's end Nolte leaves to play in The Last with his brothers.

years.h: [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] joins Frank Navetta on drums
years.p: Navetta restarts Descendents with drummer Bill Stevenson and David Nolte, now on bass. Stevenson spent his early teens working as a fisherman for [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]]'s father.

years.h: Tony Lombardo, 34, joins a band of teenagers
years.p: Bassist [[Tony Lombardo|8382eec0-45d1-4b71-a5d1-1378cee856ab]] replaces David Nolte. He was 34; Frank Navetta and Bill Stevenson were in their mid-teens.
years.xp:
Stevenson later said Lombardo looked and acted very young for his age. Lombardo went to work at the U.S. Postal Service around 1982 and stayed until he retired in 2005.

The trio rehearsed in Long Beach at the corner of 9th and Walnut, an address the band would use as an album title 42 years later.

eras.title: The class nerd becomes the logo
eras.text: A shy Mira Costa High kid named Milo Aukerman took the mic, and the band sped up into hardcore without losing its love songs. By the time the debut album came out, the singer on its cover was already packing for college.

years.h: Ride the Wild / It's a Hectic World on Orca
years.p: The first Descendents single, cut at Media Art on the band's own Orca label: Frank Navetta sings Ride the Wild, Tony Lombardo sings It's a Hectic World.
play: Ride the Wild / It's a Hectic World

years.h: [[Milo Aukerman|ce13ab7c-bf00-4894-9bc5-044ca8de134a]] takes the mic after a six-month tryout
years.p: Bill Stevenson's Mira Costa High schoolmate Milo Aukerman becomes the singer. Before him, Cecilia Loera sang with Descendents on a six-month trial.

years.h: Fat EP: Descendents go hardcore
years.p: The Fat EP puts the band in the thick of the Southern California hardcore scene, with songs that are mostly under a minute.

years.h: Bill Stevenson starts drumming for [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]
years.p: Stevenson fills in for Black Flag drummer Robo, who was stuck in England. He tries to play in both bands; Black Flag's schedule makes that impossible.
years.xp: Stevenson stayed in Black Flag until 1985 and played on My War, Slip It In, Loose Nut and more, the heart of the band's [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]]-run SST years.

years.h: Milo Goes to College, and Milo does
years.p: Recorded in June at Total Access in Redondo Beach with [[Spot|d95a08a1-80f5-4232-bdb7-4777c369f0f9]], and released on [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] and [[D. Boon|ae1757eb-8679-4cb3-8d3a-33160c953505]]'s New Alliance label. The title was literal: Milo Aukerman was leaving to study biology.
years.xp:
The cover caricature is by Jeff "Rat" Atkinson, drawn from earlier cartoons by classmate Roger Deuerlein, who had cast Aukerman as the class nerd. Stevenson picked the version with the necktie for its collegiate look.

Stevenson wrote Myage on a bass he found in a trash bin. Suburban Home is Tony Lombardo's song about wanting a normal house and a normal life. Blink-182, Sublime and Taking Back Sunday have all covered songs from the record.

years.h: Ray Cooper fills in while Milo Aukerman is at school
years.p: With Aukerman at El Camino College and then UC San Diego, [[Ray Cooper|cc1272fe-3cdf-46be-92c1-2eb950473991]] sings when Milo can't make it, and later moves to rhythm guitar.

eras.title: Fart songs, a 58-show summer, and ALL
eras.text: With Stevenson in Black Flag, the original band came apart in the most dramatic way possible. When it reformed, Descendents became a touring machine with a new Utah rhythm section, a philosophy borrowed from a fishing trip, and a singer who kept leaving for the lab.

years.h: Frank Navetta sets his gear on fire and moves to Oregon
years.p: The original band splits over touring: Stevenson wanted to, Navetta and Tony Lombardo didn't. Navetta quits by burning all his musical equipment and leaves to fish full time in Oregon.

years.h: Ray Cooper and Tony Lombardo play on as the Ascendents
years.p: While Descendents are on hiatus and Bill Stevenson tours with Black Flag, Ray Cooper and Tony Lombardo keep a band going under a one-letter-different name.

years.h: I Don't Want to Grow Up reunites the band
years.p: Milo Aukerman, Bill Stevenson, Ray Cooper and Tony Lombardo record at Music Lab in Hollywood for New Alliance. [[Mark Hoppus|fcb45d6d-bf32-4c92-8211-c47f6ed3ce75]] later called Silly Girl the first song that really altered his life.
play: I Don't Want to Grow Up

q: The biggest mistake of my life.
years.h: Tony Lombardo won't tour. Doug Carrion replaces him
years.p: Lombardo had a house, a fiancée and three years at the post office. He turned down the U.S. tour and later called it the biggest mistake of his life.
years.xp: Lombardo explained it plainly: he had just bought a house, he'd been at the post office three years, and he was engaged. Bassist [[Doug Carrion|bdc25394-8356-4bcd-9118-520f17af9333]] took the job.

years.h: Enjoy!: recorded farts and a Beach Boys cover
years.p: Cut in March and April at Radio Tokyo in Venice with Bill Stevenson producing. The band recorded real farts for several tracks; Ray Cooper drew the toilet-roll cover as "Scoob Droolins."
years.xp:
The song titles on the back were swapped for poop euphemisms like floater, sausage and loaf. When SST reissued it, it added Orgofart, which is exactly what it sounds like.

Reviews were mixed: AllMusic's Jeremy Salmon disliked the toilet humor but praised Kids, Wendy and Sour Grapes. Kids got the band's first music video.

years.h: 58 shows, 56 cities, 34 states in one summer
years.p: The Enjoy! tour covers 34 states and three Canadian provinces. When it ends, Doug Carrion and Ray Cooper both leave.
years.xp: Carrion said the split was friendly, that he wanted to keep experimenting while the band steered another way.

years.h: Stephen Egerton and Karl Alvarez arrive from Utah
years.p: Guitarist [[Stephen Egerton|2d72eb67-f40a-4fb0-af56-4187a0d30bd5]] and bassist [[Karl Alvarez|805d18ca-2f22-4e3d-8bcd-3655ead25c31]] come from the Salt Lake City band Massacre Guys. They are still the Descendents' guitarist and bassist today.

years.h: SST buys New Alliance and takes over the catalog
years.p: SST Records buys Mike Watt's New Alliance label and reissues Milo Goes to College and Enjoy! on LP, cassette and CD. The Descendents become an SST band.

years.h: All on SST, with a one-second title track
years.p: Recorded in January at Radio Tokyo. The song All lasts one second and No, All! lasts two, both written by Bill Stevenson and friend Pat McCuistion to sum up their idea of All.
years.xp: Stevenson and McCuistion came up with All on a 1980 fishing trip: the total extent, never settling for some. [[Dez Cadena|f3cd8685-7490-44ee-a5bd-cc6663ea1396]] of Black Flag sings backing vocals. Two tours followed, recorded for Liveage! (1987) and Hallraker: Live! (1989).

years.h: Milo Aukerman leaves for biochemistry
years.p: After two All tours, Aukerman quits for graduate school. Stevenson later said he toured Milo to death.

years.h: Pat McCuistion, the "fifth member," dies at sea
years.p: McCuistion, co-inventor of All, dies when his fishing boat sinks in a storm while carrying 15,000 pounds of fish. Bill Stevenson called him the band's fifth member.

eras.title: Everybody else becomes ALL
eras.text: Without Milo Aukerman, Stevenson, Egerton and Alvarez didn't hire a new Descendents singer. They changed the band's name to its own philosophy and kept going for eight years.

q: Let the Descendents be my and Milo's sacred thing.
years.h: The Descendents keep their name for Milo
years.p: Bill Stevenson, Stephen Egerton and Karl Alvarez carry on as [[ALL|e92547b5-a134-4149-af9a-c944af9e476f]], first with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] singer [[Dave Smalley|c637a12d-5f55-4b83-bef0-a56b3c1e326c]], later Scott Reynolds and Chad Price.
years.xp: Karl Alvarez drew ALL a mascot, Allroy, to fill the Milo cartoon's shoes. Stevenson kept the two bands separate out of respect for Aukerman's years in the Descendents.

years.h: Milo Aukerman wants back in, and nobody leaves ALL
years.p: Aukerman says he wants to make music again. The band decides to run both at once: Descendents with Milo, ALL with Chad Price.
years.xp: Stevenson's line on it: it's not really a reunion, they'd been together the whole time. The plan made room for Milo without pushing Chad Price out.

eras.title: Epitaph, Fat, and the original trio
eras.text: The comeback landed right as the bands Descendents inspired were selling millions. Two punk labels run by fans, Epitaph and Fat Wreck Chords, gave the band room to record only when it wanted.

years.h: Everything Sucks brings back Frank Navetta and Tony Lombardo
years.p: Recorded at Stevenson's Blasting Room in Fort Collins. Navetta writes and plays Doghouse; Lombardo plays on Eunuch Boy, the first song Milo Aukerman ever wrote.
years.xp:
It was the band's first record to chart: No. 132 on the Billboard 200 and No. 4 on Top Heatseekers. Videos for I'm the One and When I Get Old ran as European singles.

Epitaph's [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]] signed both Descendents and ALL at once and let them make records whenever they chose. The tour ran almost a year, with Bouncing Souls, [[Social Distortion|e1e05cce-3922-44e1-8f20-015abe5e309d]] and [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]] among the bands on the bills.

years.h: The original trio plays Stevenson's Stockage fest
years.p: Frank Navetta, Tony Lombardo and Bill Stevenson play together at Stockage in Fort Collins, and record songs from 1977–81 that would stay in the can for 19 years.

years.h: Cool to Be You on Fat Wreck Chords
years.p: Eight years after the last album. Bill Stevenson blamed the gap on kids and his father's death; he wrote One More Day about caring for the father he'd long been estranged from.
years.xp: The 'Merican EP came first, in February. Fat Mike, a longtime fan, was a big part of the signing. Chris Shary drew the Milo cartoon on graph paper for the cover.

eras.title: Tumors, heart attacks and a hit record
eras.text: The band's middle-aged years were a string of hospital visits, and it kept coming back louder. A brain tumor explained Stevenson's lost years, Milo got laid off into full-time punk, and the band posted its highest chart spot at 30-plus years old.

years.h: Karl Alvarez has a heart attack
years.p: Friends raise money to cover the medical bills for the Descendents, ALL and [[Lemonheads|58a53082-a629-4ff1-a44d-7492d6f6e8fb]] bassist, Punknews reported.

years.h: Frank Navetta dies at 46 of a diabetic coma
years.p: Navetta fell ill over a few days. Bill Stevenson said he went into a diabetic coma and died in his sleep without coming to.

years.cap: Bill Stevenson back behind the kit
years.h: A brain tumor removed, and Descendents play again
years.p: Bill Stevenson has a brain tumor, growing since around 2008, surgically removed; it had sapped his motivation and caused weight gain. The same year the band returns for a run of shows.
years.xp: He also had surgery to remove a blood clot from one lung. Milo Aukerman called the shows one-offs, fit into vacation time from his biochemistry job, not a real reformation.

years.h: Filmage premieres in Toronto
years.p: Deedle LaCour and Matt Riggle's documentary on Descendents and ALL premieres at the Bloor Hot Docs cinema during NXNE, with [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] and [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] among 40-plus interviews.

years.h: Tony Lombardo onstage at Riot Fest
years.p: Thirty years after turning down the tour, Lombardo joins the Descendents for their Riot Fest sets.

years.h: Milo Aukerman quits science after a DuPont layoff
years.p: Aukerman says he's burned out on biochemistry and was laid off from DuPont. For the first time, he's a full-time Descendent.

years.h: Hypercaffium Spazzinate hits No. 20
years.p: The band's highest Billboard 200 peak ever, 34 years after its first LP. Karl Alvarez wrote Feel This after his mother died.
years.xp: In the UK the title drew boycott calls from music outlets and disability advocates over the word spaz. A San Diego brewery later released a Descendents IPA named after a track on it.

years.h: Bill Stevenson has open-heart surgery
years.p: Another operation for the drummer, on top of his earlier tumor and lung surgeries.

years.h: 9th & Walnut: the 1977 songs finally recorded
years.p: Named for the Long Beach corner of the first rehearsal room. The 2002 tracks by Frank Navetta, Tony Lombardo and Bill Stevenson get Milo Aukerman's vocals, sung at home in Delaware during the pandemic.

years.h: Milo Aukerman's heart attack cancels Europe
years.p: Aukerman has a mild heart attack and surgery. Five European dates, Barcelona to Leicester, are canceled; the band says he's expected to fully recover.
